finding.claim: HIGH. The /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get and copies the full response body back to the caller. There is no scheme or host validation, and redirects are followed by default. An unauthenticated attacker can make the server request loopback, RFC-1918 or cloud metadata addresses (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/) and read the result. Redirect risk: yes (default http.Client follows up to 10 redirects). Fix: parse the URL, restrict the scheme to http/https, check u.Hostname() against a strict allowlist before the call, and use a client with CheckRedirect that re-validates each hop or returns http.ErrUseLastResponse. Optionally resolve the hostname and block loopback, private and link-local IPs.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `target`: r.URL.Query().Get("target") at main.go:15 on the public route /fetch (registered at main.go:41, served on :8080 at main.go:43)
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the response body streamed back via io.Copy(w, resp.Body) at main.go:22 (full-read SSRF)

trace.note: target := r.URL.Query().Get("target") — attacker-controlled value read from the query string
http.Get(target) — value used as the full URL (host and scheme included) with no transformation or check; default client follows redirects
io.Copy(w, resp.Body) — upstream response returned to the attacker, so this is not blind SSRF
http.HandleFunc("/fetch", fetch) — handler registered on the default mux and exposed on :8080 (main.go:43, all interfaces)

finding.guards_checked: The `allowed` map (main.go:9-12) is not consulted anywhere in fetch(). There is no scheme check, no hostname check, no IP or CIDR block, no custom http.Client or CheckRedirect, and no authentication or middleware on the route. No in-repo egress controls exist. The only other handler, safeFetch (/safe, main.go:25-38), is a separate function and does not protect this route.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` directly to http.Get with no scheme or host check (the `allowed` map at main.go:9-12 is only used in safeFetch at main.go:27), and main.go:22 returns the response body, on a public route registered at main.go:41 and served on :8080 at main.go:43.
